purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and service program for the authoritative ruined roadside diner asset, preserving a recognizable roadside food-service building with customer dining, counter service, commercial kitchen, storage, sanitation, deliveries, utilities, parking, signage, terrain seating and coherent damage behavior.
ground_program: roadside entrance, parking and pedestrian approach form a legible arrival sequence without forcing customers through delivery or refuse areas
public entrance leads into a dining room with booth, table or counter seating arranged around usable circulation rather than decorative furniture blocking aisles
service counter connects customer-facing ordering or payment space to the commercial kitchen and pass-through without requiring staff to cross the public dining floor for routine service
commercial kitchen contains a believable preparation, cooking, washing and cold-storage sequence with ventilation and utility connections appropriate to food service
dry storage, refrigeration, staff service space and refuse handling sit behind or beside the kitchen with a direct back-of-house delivery route
public sanitation is reachable from the dining area without crossing active food-preparation zones
mechanical, electrical, grease, water and exhaust systems are represented as serviceable infrastructure rather than inaccessible decorative blocks
parking, curbs, drainage, slab transitions, sign foundations and any retaining features seat the diner into terrain without floating paving, buried doors or disconnected road elevations
upper_program: roof structure supports exhaust hoods, vents, signs and mechanical equipment with plausible curbs, frames or service platforms
any rooftop equipment has a credible maintenance access path and does not rely on public architectural stairs unless the space is intentionally occupiable
freestanding or roof-mounted roadside signage uses foundations, mast or frame support appropriate to its visible height and wind exposure
any occupied second-floor or mezzanine area uses supported stairs, landings and guard relationships rather than equipment ladders
circulation: customers can move from parking to entrance, seating, counter and sanitation without unavoidable conflicts with kitchen or delivery traffic
staff circulation connects counter, kitchen, wash area, cold and dry storage, sanitation and service exit as a compact back-of-house loop
delivery circulation reaches food storage and kitchen support spaces without passing through the public dining room
refuse and grease-service access remains separated from the principal customer entrance and outdoor seating where present
maintenance access reaches electrical, plumbing, refrigeration, exhaust and roof-service equipment
equipment-only ladders do not substitute for architectural stairs in occupied spaces
damage_constraints: the ruined derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a roadside diner through surviving dining-room, service-counter, kitchen, roadside-sign and parking relationships
favor localized roof failure, storefront glazing loss, kitchen fire, vehicle impact, sign damage, water intrusion, vandalism and vegetation intrusion over uniform random deletion
roof or sign collapse must follow identifiable structural failure and resolve attached lights, ducts, fascia and supports so floating fragments are not left behind
kitchen damage may expose equipment and utilities but should preserve enough of the preparation-cooking-service relationship to communicate the former function
dining-room damage should retain at least one viable public exploration path from entrance toward counter or seating
parking, curbs, drainage and road connection should remain spatially coherent after damage rather than becoming disconnected slabs
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master
